Based on the search results, here's what I found regarding GRE coaching and whether it's a waste of money:

## Mixed Perspectives on Value

Experts and students say time and money invested in test-prep courses for graduate admission exams could be a waste. However, the consensus isn't entirely negative—it depends on individual circumstances.

## When Coaching May Not Be Necessary

If you have the will to study on your own, you could save the money, as the effectiveness of courses depends on how much effort students put into it. Additionally, you can achieve over 320 points on the GRE exam without any instruction or coaching guidance, and if you study from good GRE books, you can get good grades.

## When Coaching Might Help

What's nice about classes is that they make you do the work. Also, students who need a structured environment or those who can't study on their own might benefit from a prep course.

## Cost Considerations

Companies like Kaplan and The Princeton Review charge up to $4,000 for help preparing for the GRE. For those concerned about cost, The Educational Testing Service sends each registered student a free practice test with the answers.

The search results don't include specific Reddit discussions, but the overall takeaway is that GRE coaching's value depends on your self-discipline, learning style, and access to quality self-study materials.

I found several relevant results about paid GRE courses and their effectiveness. Here's what the search revealed:

**Common Issues with Paid GRE Courses:**

Some customers of Princeton Review complained that though they saw improvement in scores during the course, those improvements didn't carry over to the real exam. Similarly, working through Kaplan questions using Kaplan-taught strategies may improve your score on Kaplan's practice exams, but not necessarily on the real GRE.

**Effectiveness Varies:**

The effectiveness of GRE prep courses depends heavily on individual circumstances. The effectiveness of the courses depends on how much effort students put into it and how dedicated they are. Price doesn't indicate effectiveness, and marketing materials tell you even less.

**Student Perspectives:**

Some students feel paid courses aren't worth the investment. One student said he didn't think a course would be much more beneficial than free sources and could do just as well on his own.

**Who Might Benefit:**

Students who need a structured environment or those who can't study on their own might benefit from a prep course. Additionally, courses may be worth the investment if you are concerned/anxious, or definitely want to get the highest score you can muster.
